title: Blood Orange, Fennel & Avocado Salad
steps: Slice the peel and pith off the oranges with a knife, then cut into rounds. Save the juice from the board.
Toss fennel and arugula with olive oil, the saved juice, and a pinch of salt.
Layer on a platter with orange rounds and avocado. Finish with flaky salt, pepper, olives, and the fennel fronds.

title: Charred Cauliflower Tacos with Cabbage-Lime Slaw
ingredients: 1 head cauliflower, cut into small florets
2 tbsp oil, 1 tsp each cumin and smoked paprika
Corn tortillas, cilantro, crema or salsa
steps: Toss cauliflower with oil, spices, and salt. Roast at 450°F for 25 minutes until charred at the edges.
Meanwhile, toss cabbage and radish with lime juice and a big pinch of salt. Let it sit and soften.
Warm tortillas on a dry pan. Fill with cauliflower, slaw, cilantro, and crema.

title: Meyer Lemon & Kale Pasta
ingredients: 1 bunch kale or chard, stems removed, chopped
steps: Boil pasta in well-salted water. Add the kale for the last 2 minutes.
Meanwhile, soften the leek in butter over medium-low heat, about 8 minutes.
Drain, saving 1 cup of pasta water. Toss everything with the leeks, lemon zest and juice, a splash of pasta water, and a lot of Parmesan.

title: Pea, Fava & Mint Smash on Toast
steps: Blanch the favas for 1 minute, shock them in ice water, and slip off the skins. Blanch the peas for 90 seconds.
Gently cook the green garlic in olive oil for 2 minutes. Add the peas and favas, then roughly mash with a fork, mint, lemon, and salt.
Toast the bread, spread with ricotta, pile on the smash, and finish with olive oil.

title: Grilled Artichokes with Lemon Aioli
ingredients: 1/2 cup mayo, 1 garlic clove grated, zest and juice of 1 lemon
steps: Trim the tops and stems, halve the artichokes, and scoop out the fuzzy chokes. Steam or boil for 15–20 minutes until a knife slides into the heart.
Brush with oil, season, and grill cut-side down over high heat until charred, about 5 minutes.
Stir together the aioli ingredients. Serve warm.

title: Ensalada de Nopales
ingredients: 2 tomatoes (or a handful of cherry tomatoes), diced
Cilantro, lime, salt, crumbled queso fresco
steps: Simmer the diced nopales in salted water with a chunk of onion for 10–15 minutes until they turn olive green. Drain and rinse well to remove the slime.
Toss with onion, chile, tomato, cilantro, lime juice, and salt.
Top with queso fresco. Good on tostadas or as a side.

title: Oxnard Strawberry Shortcakes
ingredients: 2 baskets strawberries, sliced, plus 2 tbsp sugar
2 cups flour, 1 tbsp baking powder, 3 tbsp sugar, 1/2 tsp salt
6 tbsp cold butter, 3/4 cup cream (plus more for whipping)
steps: Toss the berries with sugar and let them sit for 30 minutes until syrupy.
Cut the butter into the dry ingredients, stir in the cream, pat into a 1-inch slab, and cut 6 rounds. Bake at 425°F for 15 minutes.
Split the biscuits and fill with berries and softly whipped cream.

title: Esquites (Street Corn Salad)
ingredients: 4 ears of corn, kernels cut off
3 tbsp mayo or crema, juice of 1 lime
Cotija, chili powder or Tajín, cilantro
steps: Char the corn in butter in a hot cast-iron pan without stirring too often, about 6 minutes.
Stir in the jalapeño for 1 minute, then take it off the heat.
Toss with mayo, lime, cotija, chili powder, and cilantro. Serve warm in cups.

title: Heirloom Tomato & Peach Salad
ingredients: 3 ripe heirloom tomatoes, cut into wedges
Olive oil, sherry vinegar, flaky salt
steps: Salt the tomatoes and let them sit for 5 minutes.
Arrange with the peaches and burrata. Drizzle with oil and a splash of vinegar.
Tear the basil over the top and finish with pepper. Eat immediately.

title: Campfire Stone Fruit Foil Packs
ingredients: 4 peaches, plums, or pluots, halved and pitted
2 tbsp butter, 2 tbsp brown sugar, pinch of cinnamon
steps: Divide the fruit among 4 foil squares. Top each with butter, brown sugar, and cinnamon.
Seal tightly and set on hot coals or a grill grate for 10–12 minutes.
Open carefully because of the steam. Great with graham crackers or vanilla yogurt.

title: Squash Blossom Quesadillas
ingredients: 12 squash blossoms, stems and pistils removed
steps: Sauté the zucchini and poblano for 3 minutes. Add the blossoms for 30 seconds until they wilt.
Fill the tortillas with cheese and the vegetables, then fold.
Cook on a griddle or camp stove until crisp and melty. Serve with salsa.

title: Oak Glen Apple Dutch Baby
ingredients: 3 tbsp butter, 2 tbsp brown sugar, cinnamon
3 eggs, 2/3 cup milk, 2/3 cup flour, pinch of salt
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F with a 10-inch cast-iron skillet inside.
Blend the eggs, milk, flour, and salt. Melt the butter in the hot skillet and cook the apples with sugar and cinnamon for 3 minutes.
Pour the batter over the apples and bake for 18–20 minutes until puffed and golden. Dust with powdered sugar.

title: Fuyu Persimmon & Pomegranate Salad
steps: Toss the greens lightly with oil, vinegar, and salt.
Layer with the persimmon, pomegranate seeds, and pecans.
Add shaved Parmesan or crumbled goat cheese if you like.

title: Kabocha Coconut Curry Soup
ingredients: 1 onion, 3 garlic cloves, 1 thumb of ginger
steps: Soften the onion, garlic, and ginger in oil. Stir in the curry paste for 1 minute.
Add the squash, sweet potato, coconut milk, and stock. Simmer for 25 minutes until tender.
Blend until smooth. Season with lime and salt, and top with cilantro.

title: One-Pot Camp Chile Verde Beans
ingredients: 4 green chiles (Anaheim or Hatch-style), charred and chopped
1 lb tomatillos or green tomatoes, chopped
steps: Char the chiles over the campfire or burner. Peel and chop them.
In a Dutch oven, soften the onion and garlic, then add the tomatillos and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the beans, chiles, and spices. Simmer for 15 minutes and serve with cilantro and warm tortillas.
